summary: Stage/admin secret sent as Bearer over PLAINTEXT HTTP to the token endpoint (defeats any transport confidentiality on a hostile LAN).
scenario: SPOTIFY_TOKEN_URL derives from HTTP_URL which defaults to http:// (README: ':8777/tcp — plain HTTP'). The stage GETs the token with Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_SECRET> in cleartext. Anyone sniffing the conference LAN captures the admin secret and can then impersonate stage/admin roles. Bundle-inlining of VITE_STAGE_SECRET is acknowledged/unavoidable, but shipping it over cleartext HTTP is an additional, avoidable leak beyond the trusted device.
suggested_fix: Serve the token/cert endpoints over HTTPS (TLS) and require VITE_HTTP_URL to be https in non-dev; do not transmit the shared secret over an unencrypted channel.

summary: No WebTransport reconnect: on any connection drop the stage wedges offline until a manual page reload.
scenario: connect() is called exactly once in a mount-time useEffect. When the QUIC/WebTransport session drops (transient wifi blip, server restart), client.handleClose fires onState(false) so the ConnDot flips to 'offline', but nothing ever retries. For a multi-hour unattended conference game the projector silently and permanently loses all state/audio commands after a single network hiccup.
suggested_fix: Add reconnect-with-backoff in useGame's onState(false) path (re-run the connect + hello sequence, re-registering handlers), or a reconnect loop in the client wrapper; cap retries and surface status.

summary: No React ErrorBoundary + unvalidated server-frame casts: a malformed/unexpected frame throws during render and white-screens the whole projector with no recovery.
scenario: Server frames are cast (e.d as BoardData / MaskedRevealData / etc.) with zero shape validation, and there is no top-level ErrorBoundary. A frame missing an expected array (e.g. board.cells undefined, or maskedReveal.artist not iterable) makes a view throw during render; without a boundary the entire stage unmounts to a blank screen and cannot recover without a reload. An unattended projector then shows nothing for the rest of the event.
suggested_fix: Wrap <App/> in an ErrorBoundary that renders a fallback and keeps retrying, and defensively coerce/guard array fields (cells, mask arrays, players) before iterating.

summary: WebTransport server-cert hash is fetched over plaintext HTTP and blindly trusted, so a LAN MITM can substitute a hash and defeat cert pinning.
scenario: CERT_HASH_URL is http://host:8777/cert-hash. The returned SHA-256 is passed straight into WebTransport serverCertificateHashes. On a hostile conference LAN an attacker who MITMs the cleartext /cert-hash response supplies their own cert's hash, then MITMs the QUIC session too — the pinning becomes trust-on-first-response over an unauthenticated channel. On fetch failure the code returns undefined and connects with NO pinning at all.
suggested_fix: Deliver the cert hash over an authenticated/HTTPS channel (or bake it at build time); on fetch failure fail closed in dev rather than dropping pinning silently.

summary: Fire-and-forget client.send() in audio state callbacks produces unhandled promise rejections once the transport is closed.
scenario: After the WebTransport session drops, this.writer is undefined so GameClient.send() throws 'not connected'. Because the call is `void`ed, every player_state_changed event (which keeps firing from the local Spotify SDK) yields an unhandled rejection, spamming the console and potentially the global unhandledrejection handler while the stage is offline.
suggested_fix: Guard sends on connection state (skip when disconnected) or attach a .catch to the voided sends; combine with the reconnect fix in uistage-2.
